stacks.name: AI Dev Server
stacks.goal: Autonomous software development with memory, observability, browser testing and model routing.
notes: Use OpenHands as an alternative autonomous coding engine.
Use qdrant/qdrant when vector retrieval becomes a first-class requirement.

stacks.name: XAUUSD Research
stacks.goal: Robust Gold/USD research from data ingestion to backtest, ML, risk and execution.
notes: Prefer out-of-sample profit robustness over win rate.
Model spread, slippage and session/macro regimes explicitly.

stacks.name: Vector Animation Android
stacks.goal: Create and deploy high-quality vector animation on Android.
notes: Use Spine or Rive-style runtimes for richer interactive animation.

stacks.name: Full-stack Web App
stacks.goal: Modern full-stack product with strong UI, API, data and test coverage.
notes: Swap Supabase for FastAPI + Postgres when backend control matters more than speed.

stacks.name: Android Product
stacks.goal: Production Android app with modern UI, backend integration and testing.
notes: Use React Native/Expo or Flutter instead when cross-platform speed matters more than native architecture.

stacks.name: Game Production
stacks.goal: Cross-platform game with rendering, backend and ecosystem tooling.
notes: For Java ecosystems, libgdx/libgdx is the main alternative.

stacks.name: Roblox Studio Agent Production
stacks.goal: Build and polish Roblox Studio gameplay with Luau coding agents, iterative playtesting, animation and performance diagnostics.
notes: Roblox Studio authoring and instrumented playtests require a supported desktop environment; an Android phone alone cannot run Studio.
Treat third-party agent actions as untrusted until scripts, assets, permissions and game behavior are reviewed.
Roqer is AGPL-3.0; assess deployment and redistribution obligations before integration.
Prefer built-in Roblox Studio MCP when available; this stack documents an alternative tested-tooling option, not an official dependency.

stacks.name: Godot Gameplay and VFX
stacks.goal: Create Godot games with engine-supported gameplay, shaders, visual effects and agent-assisted GDScript iteration.
notes: Use demo project shader examples as references, not as finished studio-quality scenes; verify each game's rendering in engine.
Review source, compatibility and privileges of external Godot MCP extensions before connecting them to a production project.
Engine-level development requires desktop tooling; running a finished Android export is a different workflow.

stacks.name: Authorized Security Validation
stacks.goal: Defensive validation and authorized security assessment workflows.
notes: Use only in authorized environments and keep scope controls fail-closed.
